extracted.intended_audience: middle and high school students and their families applying to the Berkeley Math Circle MTRW program
extracted.subtask_description: Information and requirements for applying, enrolling, and participating in the Berkeley Math Circle 'Math Taught the Right Way' (MTRW) program for middle and high school students. Covers curriculum expectations, eligibility by grade/prerequisite, application phases and deadlines, payment and refund policies, attendance/format commitments, and assessment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program rigor and curriculum scope
rubrics_metrics.description: MTRW is a program ... that is intellectually demanding, and it tests and encourages the mental development of students in a content-rich and challenging environment. The program does NOT conform to generic U.S. labels of math classes (e.g., Algebra 1, Algebra 2, etc.), but instead interweaves algebra and geometry with general problem-solving and writing skills. By the end of 9th grade, MTRW surpasses the regular U.S. math curriculum, in breadth, and more importantly, in depth and rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning to "read and write mathematics" is a skill that is emphasized at MTRW as the basis for communicating mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Most instructors at the MTRW have PhD, MA, or BA degrees in math or other related degrees in science and are distinguished teachers at the Berkeley Math Circle, universities, and renowned middle and high schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly homework and subject assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: MTRW students submit homework to be graded each week in each of three subjects: algebra, geometry, and proofs/problem solving. There are final exams in each subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report cards include the percentage of successfully completed regular and bonus work, as well as statistics for the corresponding classes, a list of top performers, and some special awards from instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria: academic qualifications and demonstrated dedication
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection process is based on high academic qualifications and a timely and complete application, including payment sent through PayPal upon acceptance. We will select only those who have shown dedication and growth in the program. We also expect to accept some very strong new students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readmission for current students is not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application phases, deadlines, and decision schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are handled in phases with specific windows and decision dates (Phase 1: Now through Tuesday, April 21st — decisions April 24th; Phase 2: Wednesday, April 22nd thru Tuesday, April 28th — decisions (pending space) May 1st; Phase 3: Wednesday, April 29th and thereafter — decisions sent as space allows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoices are due by specified dates (e.g., Phase 1 invoice due by Monday, April 27th at 12pm; Phase 2 invoice due by Monday, May 4th at 12pm).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely payment and invoice rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments will be collected only from admitted students after we sign the agreement for this fall. Payments must be made online within 48 hours of the acceptance email and invoice being sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO NOT SEND PAYMENTS before you have received such an email.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-refund policy after enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: Once enrolled and students have paid their enrollment fees, no refunds will be provided to families, regardless of changed personal circumstances or if sessions move between in-person and online modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No refunds will be provided for any reason after a student is enrolled in the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance and commitment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Families must commit to attending in-person AND any online sessions of MTRW in Fall 2026, regardless of when/whether a change of mode may occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should only enroll if they can regularly attend classes live, regardless of whether they are held online or on campus. If you are not sure you would like to participate in MTRW, you should NOT apply. If you are applying to MTRW just to "try it out," you should not apply. Spaces should be given to the most dedicated families who are ready to commit to rigorous mathematical education and have no doubts about their commitment, schedule, or situation in Fall 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional mode contingency and possible splitting of siblings
rubrics_metrics.description: MTRW sessions in the Fall 2026 semester are anticipated to be held IN-PERSON, possibly with occasional online sessions as needed. Depending on local and/or national guidelines, masking or even online classes may be re-introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is possible, but unlikely, that a move to remote classes would be necessary for some MTRW groups but not for others, in which case siblings may be split between attending on campus and attending online at the same time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group placement by grade and prerequisite completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief descriptions specify intended grade levels and prerequisites for each group (6A: intended for 6th graders or motivated 7th graders who lack some background; 7A: intended for 7th graders and advanced 6th graders who successfully completed 6B MTRW; 8A: intended for 8th graders and advanced 7th graders who have successfully completed the MTRW 7B material; 9A: intended for 9th-12th graders and advanced 8th graders who have successfully completed the MTRW 8B material; 9A Proofs-only: restricted only to 10th-12th graders or students who have completed the MTRW 8B material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final exam scheduling and no-makeup policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Exams will be conducted during the last two weeks of classes, at a schedule and in modes (in person or take-home), as determined by the instructors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Families cannot request make-up Finals or alternative final exams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity and urgency to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically, the program fills quite quickly, with some groups reaching capacity in less than a week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We are currently accepting applications through May 8th, 2026. Remember that the space in the MTRW is very limited to the classrooms that we receive and all slots fill up quite quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication/contact policy during application
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT contact MTRW staff with non-emergency questions at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignoring this policy may hurt your admission chances. We do NOT reply to email inquiries as we do NOT have the resources to answer questions from hundreds of families via email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee schedule by group
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are the fees for the MTRW Fall 2026 Program: $910 for the 6A, 7A, 8A, or 9A full programs; $303 for the 9A Proofs only program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments must be made online within 48 hours of the acceptance email and invoice being sent; DO NOT SEND PAYMENTS before you have received such an email.
